newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government says reshuffle not on agenda.
newsitem.headline: French government says reshuffle not on agenda.

text.p: The French government on Tuesday dismissed speculation that a cabinet reshuffle was under consideration.
"I can tell you that a reshuffle is not on the agenda," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told RTL radio in an interview.
"The decision on changing the government naturally belongs to the President (Jacques Chirac). I can tell you that as far as the government is concerned, a reshuffle is not on the agenda."

Chirac's determination to stick to austerity policies to ensure France qualifies for a single European currency, despite deepening unpopularity, has led to talk of a reshuffle to breathe new life into Prime Minister Alain Juppe's flagging government.
Education Minister Francois Bayrou hinted on Sunday that a reshuffle was under consideration "so that the (ruling) coalition's composition is reflected in government".

One of the expected beneficiaries, ex-budget minister Nicolas Sarkozy, suggested a shakeup was not imminent. "My belief is that there's no urgency in reshuffling the cabinet or changing faces," he said.
